title: Diamond DA40 180 — Emergency Procedures
description: Emergency procedures for the Diamond DA40 with 180-hp Lycoming IO-360 engine and constant-speed propeller. Memory items are marked accordingly. Contains no numeric limitations; all airspeeds and power settings must come from the specific aircraft POH/AFM. The IO-360 is fuel-injected — there is no carburetor and no carburetor heat system; carburetor ice is not applicable. A note is included in the carb-ice section for reference. DA40-specific considerations: canopy-style door that must be unlatched before forced landing; T-tail pitch characteristics at slow speed; composite airframe.

source.notes: No manufacturer document consulted. Written from general familiarity with the Diamond DA40, Lycoming IO-360 fuel-injected engine, and constant-speed propeller emergency procedures.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, or other numeric limits — all such values must come from the specific aircraft POH/AFM.
Emergency checklists must be practiced and the memory items memorized. This file is an aide-memoire only. Aviate first, then navigate, then communicate.
Avionics configuration (G1000 vs steam-gauge) affects the information available during emergencies. Verify all procedures against the specific aircraft POH and supplements.

rights.notes: Diamond Aircraft POH/AFM remains under copyright. This file is independently authored and does not reproduce the wording or item selection of any manufacturer document.

items.text: Master switches (battery and alternator)
Airspeed — increase to maximum glide within structural limits to help extinguish fire through airflow
Emergency landing — initiate forced landing immediately; do not attempt restart
Declare emergency — squawk 7700; transmit position and intentions on 121.5 if able
Canopy — do not open in flight (fire and smoke inhalation hazard); delay until landing and evacuation
Mixture
Fuel selector
Throttle — advance fully open to draw fire back into engine compartment
Ignition switch
Master switches
Canopy — unlatch and open; evacuate aircraft immediately
Fire extinguisher — direct at base of fire if safe to do so; do not linger near aircraft
Emergency services — call 911 or airport authority; do not attempt to fly the aircraft
Master switches (battery and alternator)
All electrical switches — avionics, lights, pitot heat, fans
Vents / fresh air — increase airflow to dilute smoke; do not open canopy in flight unless specifically directed by POH
Land as soon as possible — declare emergency; smoke and fumes impair pilot performance rapidly
Circuit breakers — if source is identifiable, pull relevant breaker; do not reset a tripped breaker if fire is suspected
Battery master — may be restored selectively if radio contact is needed for approach; re-evaluate whether smoke resumes
items.response: RESTORE ONLY IF NECESSARY AND SAFE

items.text: Squawk 7700 — declare emergency on 121.5 if other comms are lost
Oil pressure — confirm indication is abnormally low or zero; cross-check oil temperature for confirming trend
Throttle — reduce to minimum power needed to maintain controlled flight; minimize engine load
Land immediately — engine failure is imminent if pressure is at or near zero; select best available field now
Mixture — enrich if not already; do not lean a potentially overheating engine
Declare emergency — squawk 7700; advise ATC of situation and intention
Engine instruments — monitor CHT and oil temperature for continued degradation; be prepared for sudden seizure
If oil temperature also rising rapidly — treat as imminent engine failure; do not delay forced landing

The Lycoming IO-360 installed in the DA40 180 is fuel-injected. It has no carburetor and no carburetor heat system. Carburetor icing cannot occur. If unexplained power loss occurs, refer to the Engine Failure in Flight checklist.
Best glide speed — establish and maintain throughout; the DA40's composite airframe glides efficiently
Landing site — select the best available field considering length, surface, slope, obstacles, and wind direction
Squawk 7700 — declare emergency on current frequency or 121.5
Fuel selector
Mixture
Propeller — if engine windmilling, consider setting prop full coarse (low RPM) per POH to reduce drag if time permits
Ignition switch — off when landing is assured
Master switches — off before impact to reduce electrical fire risk; leave on until confident landing is achievable
Canopy latch — UNLATCH prior to touchdown to ensure exit is available after impact; do not open in flight
Seat belts and shoulder harnesses — as tight as possible on all occupants
Flaps — extend per POH recommendation for terrain type; full flaps for short fields, partial for rough terrain
Touchdown — aim for far edge of field; fly to the ground; do not stall high; T-tail — maintain positive control through flare; be alert for pitch sensitivity near stall
After stopping — canopy open; evacuate aircraft promptly and move upwind away from fuel
